abstract: Pollen tube reception (PTR) is essential for fertilization and can act as a prezygotic barrier in interspecific crosses. While core female components such as LORELEI (LRE) and FERONIA (FER) mediate conspecific PTR, their roles in heterospecific compatibility remain unclear. Here, we investigated how LRE sequence variation influences PTR outcomes with heterospecific pollen in Brassicaceae. In Arabidopsis thaliana, PTR frequently failed when ovules were pollinated with Arabidopsis lyrata or Sisymbrium irio, and loss of LRE or FER further increased pollen tube overgrowth in a pollen-species-dependent manner. Complementation of lre ovules with LRE orthologs showed distinct, donor-dependent effects: AlyLRE and SiLRE produced modest and variable improvements with A. lyrata pollen, whereas SiLRE consistently and markedly improved reception of S. irio pollen. Evolutionary analyses indicated relaxed purifying selection in the LRE lineage relative to its paralog LLG1 and nominated residues 47 and 120 as candidates for functional divergence. Consistent with this, the Lineage II-associated R120T substitution enhanced reception of S. irio pollen while partially reducing conspecific PTR. In addition, the ancestral-state E47P-R120G combination also improved heterospecific PTR without measurably compromising conspecific function. Together, these results indicate that LRE sequence diversification can modulate female-side compatibility with pollen tubes from different evolutionary lineages, potentially by altering how pollen tube-derived signals are sensed and transduced during reception.
